prompt: Tell me about yourself.
translation: Ceritakan tentang diri Anda.
followUps: Which part of your background is most relevant to this role?
Which project are you proudest of, and why?
skeleton: Present role and years of experience
One flagship result with a number
The strength you are known for
Why this role, in one sentence
modelAnswer: I'm a full-stack engineer with seven years of experience building web and mobile products. In my last project I led a five-person team rebuilding a government investment dashboard, cutting report processing from two days to four hours for about 50,000 users. My strength is turning messy requirements into a system that ships. I'm interested in this role because it combines backend depth with product-facing frontend work, which is where I do my best work.

keyPhrases.target: cut processing time from two days to four hours
keyPhrases.note: Concrete result with a before and after.

rubricPoints: States current role and years of experience
Includes at least one measurable result
redFlags: Recites the CV line by line
Talks for more than two minutes
culturalNote: 60-90 seconds. End with why this role, not with your hobbies.

prompt: Why are you interested in this role?
translation: Mengapa Anda tertarik dengan posisi ini?
followUps: What do you know about our product?
What would you change about it?
skeleton: Name one concrete thing about the product or team
Connect it to a problem you have solved
State what you want to learn here
modelAnswer: The role connects the two things I do best: backend systems and user-facing interfaces. I looked at your product and noticed the reporting flow still requires manual exports; that is the kind of problem I solved in my last two projects. I also want to work on a team that ships weekly, because that pace keeps my decisions honest.

keyPhrases.target: the reporting flow still requires manual exports
keyPhrases.note: Shows you actually used the product.

rubricPoints: Shows specific knowledge of the company
Connects the role to personal experience
redFlags: Only says the company is famous
No link to your own work
Talks only about salary or location
culturalNote: Research one real detail. Generic enthusiasm is the most common rejection reason.

prompt: What are your strengths?
translation: Apa kelebihan Anda?
followUps: Can you give me an example of that?
How would a teammate describe that strength?
skeleton: Give a short example with a result
modelAnswer: My strength is breaking a vague problem into steps a team can execute. When we had to migrate authentication without downtime, I split it into audit, dual-write, gradual cutover, and cleanup. About 50,000 users moved with no reported outages, and the checklist became the team standard.

keyPhrases.target: without downtime
keyPhrases.note: Names the constraint that made the work hard.

culturalNote: One strength with evidence beats five adjectives.

prompt: What is your biggest weakness?
translation: Apa kekurangan Anda?
followUps: What have you done to improve it?
When did it last affect your work?
skeleton: Describe the system you now use
modelAnswer: I tend to go deep on technical details before updating stakeholders. I noticed it when a design decision sat with me for a week and delayed a client review. Now I send a short Friday note with decisions and open risks, and I timebox exploration to two days before asking for input.

keyPhrases.target: I timebox exploration to two days
keyPhrases.note: Shows a concrete mechanism, not a promise.

redFlags: Uses the perfectionist cliché without a mechanism
Chooses a weakness that is fatal to the role
culturalNote: Pick a real, non-fatal weakness and show the system you built around it.

prompt: Why are you leaving your current job?
translation: Mengapa Anda ingin resign dari pekerjaan sekarang?
followUps: What would you miss about it?
What would make you stay?
modelAnswer: I've learned a lot about regulated systems and stakeholder management there. What's missing is the pace and scale of a product team that ships weekly. I want to work where experiments are measured and architecture decisions are revisited with data, and that is what this role offers.

keyPhrases.target: What's missing is the pace and scale
keyPhrases.note: Forward-looking, not a complaint.

rubricPoints: Consistent with why you applied here
redFlags: Contradicts your motivation for this role
culturalNote: Never criticise people. Frame the gap, not the grievance.

prompt: Tell me about a time you handled a difficult deadline.
translation: Ceritakan pengalaman Anda menghadapi tenggat yang ketat.
followUps: What did you cut, and how did you decide?
Who did you tell, and when?
skeleton: What you cut, changed, or escalated
modelAnswer: We had a two-week window to ship a compliance feature for a government client, and I owned the API and the migration. On day four I realised the legacy data cleanup was underestimated, so I flagged it immediately, cut one non-critical report, and paired with QA on a staged rollout. We shipped one day late with zero data issues.

keyPhrases.target: flagged it immediately
keyPhrases.note: Shows early escalation, not heroics.

culturalNote: One missed deadline can be a strong answer if the escalation is early and specific.

prompt: Describe a conflict with a colleague and how you resolved it.
translation: Bagaimana Anda menyelesaikan konflik dengan rekan kerja?
followUps: What would you do differently?
How is your relationship now?
skeleton: What you did to understand the other side
The decision rule you agreed on
modelAnswer: A QA lead and I disagreed on whether a flaky test should block a release. I asked for 30 minutes to map user impact per failing case, and we agreed on a shared severity rubric. We shipped the critical fixes first, and that rubric became our team's triage standard.

keyPhrases.target: map user impact per failing case
keyPhrases.note: Moves the argument from opinion to criteria.

redFlags: Portrays the other person as irrational
Resolves it by avoiding the person
culturalNote: Focus on the decision rule, not on who was right.

prompt: Tell me about a time you failed.
translation: Ceritakan pengalaman gagal Anda.
followUps: What did you change afterwards?
Did the same problem happen again?
skeleton: The failure and your role in it
modelAnswer: I once released a payment change without testing the refund path. Two customers were charged twice, and I owned the fix and the apology. The root cause was that our checklist relied on memory, so I turned it into a required pull-request template. We had no repeat in the next year.

keyPhrases.target: I owned the fix and the apology
keyPhrases.note: Accountability without drama.

culturalNote: Choose a failure with real consequences and show the system you changed.

prompt: Tell me about a time you led a project.
translation: Ceritakan pengalaman Anda memimpin proyek.
followUps: How did you handle a teammate who disagreed?
What did you delegate?
skeleton: The goal and the team size
modelAnswer: I led five engineers rebuilding an investment dashboard for a ministry. I split the work by risk, ran a 15-minute daily unblock session, and kept a public decision log. We delivered two weeks early and cut report processing from two days to four hours. Two of the engineers later led their own modules.

keyPhrases.target: kept a public decision log
keyPhrases.note: Shows a repeatable leadership practice.

culturalNote: Leadership is about unblocking and decisions, not about doing everything yourself.

prompt: Walk me through the architecture of a system you built.
translation: Jelaskan arsitektur sistem yang pernah Anda bangun.
followUps: What would you change if traffic grew ten times?
Where is the single point of failure?
skeleton: The main components and data flow
modelAnswer: It was a government reporting platform: a Next.js frontend, a Spring Boot API, PostgreSQL, and a queue for heavy exports. The constraint was a strict audit trail, so every write went through the API and into an append-only event table. Exports moved to a worker to keep requests under 300 milliseconds. Today I would add read replicas earlier.

keyPhrases.target: every write went through the API
keyPhrases.note: Ties a component choice to a requirement.

culturalNote: Lead with constraints, then components, then trade-offs.

prompt: Tell me about a trade-off you made for performance.
translation: Ceritakan trade-off yang Anda ambil demi performa.
followUps: How did you measure the improvement?
What did you give up?
skeleton: The slow path and how you measured it
modelAnswer: A dashboard query took nine seconds on 200,000 rows. I added a composite index and a nightly materialised summary. It dropped to under 400 milliseconds, at the cost of data being up to one day stale for one widget. We labelled that widget with a timestamp so users understood the delay.

keyPhrases.target: at the cost of data being up to one day stale
keyPhrases.note: Names the price of the optimisation.

rubricPoints: Names the cost of the trade-off
culturalNote: A trade-off answer needs the cost, not only the win.

prompt: Describe a production incident you handled.
translation: Ceritakan insiden produksi yang pernah Anda tangani.
followUps: What was the root cause?
What changed in your process?
modelAnswer: A release caused 12 percent of API requests to fail. I was on call, so I rolled back within eight minutes and opened an incident timeline. The cause was a migration that dropped an index. We restored the index, then added a migration checklist and index monitoring. There was no repeat in six months.

keyPhrases.target: rolled back within eight minutes
keyPhrases.note: Shows action under pressure.

culturalNote: Interviewers care more about your process than about the outage itself.

prompt: You have three urgent requests and one engineer. How do you prioritize?
translation: Ada tiga permintaan mendesak dan satu engineer. Bagaimana Anda memprioritaskan?
followUps: What if the CEO owns one of them?
How do you communicate the delay?
modelAnswer: First I separate impact from urgency: what breaks, for whom, and can it be undone. Then I rank by damage per day of delay. I would fix the data-loss issue, schedule the revenue-blocking fix for tomorrow, and tell the third stakeholder the date and the reason. I confirm the ranking with my manager in writing.

keyPhrases.target: damage per day of delay
keyPhrases.note: A clear, defensible ranking rule.

culturalNote: Give a rule, then apply it to the three items.

prompt: A key feature is failing for 10% of users. How do you investigate?
translation: Fitur utama gagal untuk 10% pengguna. Bagaimana Anda menyelidikinya?
followUps: What data would you look at first?
How do you decide to roll back?
skeleton: Form a hypothesis about the common factor
modelAnswer: I would first check whether the 10 percent correlates with device, region, role, or a recent release. If it started with the last deploy, I roll back first and investigate after. Then I reproduce with one affected account, add logging if needed, and ship a fix behind a flag to a small group.

keyPhrases.target: If it started with the last deploy, I roll back first
keyPhrases.note: Prioritises restoring service.

culturalNote: State the first diagnostic cut before proposing a fix.

prompt: How would you reduce onboarding drop-off by half?
translation: Bagaimana Anda mengurangi drop-off onboarding hingga setengah?
followUps: Which step would you test first?
How would you know it worked?
skeleton: Define the funnel and the biggest drop
modelAnswer: I would map the funnel step by step and find where the largest drop happens. If it is the email verification step, I would test social login and a resumable flow for one cohort. Success is verification completion within 24 hours, measured against a holdout group before a full rollout.

keyPhrases.target: measured against a holdout group
keyPhrases.note: Shows a real experiment design.

rubricPoints: Names the funnel and the metric
redFlags: Suggests a redesign with no metric
culturalNote: Pick one step, one change, one metric.

prompt: What are your salary expectations?
translation: Berapa ekspektasi gaji Anda?
followUps: What is your minimum?
How did you arrive at that range?
modelAnswer: Based on market data for a senior role with backend and mobile scope, I'm targeting a range of 18 to 24 million gross per month, and I'm open to discussing the total package. Could you share the band for this role so we can align?

keyPhrases.target: open to discussing the total package
keyPhrases.note: Keeps the conversation alive.

rubricPoints: Gives a range, not one number
redFlags: Names a number with no basis
culturalNote: Say gross, say range, and ask for their band.

prompt: What is your notice period, and are you authorized to work here?
translation: Berapa lama notice period Anda, dan bagaimana status izin kerja Anda?
followUps: Would you need relocation support?
When could you start?
modelAnswer: My notice period is one month, so I could start in early March. I currently hold an Indonesian passport and would need a work visa for this role; I have the documents ready and can start the process immediately. I am also open to relocating.

keyPhrases.target: would need a work visa
keyPhrases.note: Honest and specific about authorization.

redFlags: Promises a start date you cannot meet
culturalNote: Never guess about visa status; say what you know and what you will handle.

prompt: Do you have any questions for us?
translation: Apa pertanyaan Anda untuk kami?
followUps: Apa yang ingin Anda ketahui sebelum menerima tawaran?
Apa pertanyaan Anda tentang tim ini?
skeleton: Ask about success in the first six months
Ask about the hardest current problem
modelAnswer: Yes, three things. What does success look like in the first six months? How do product and engineering make technical trade-offs? And what is the hardest problem the team wants to solve this year?

keyPhrases.target: What does success look like in the first six months?
keyPhrases.note: Signals you plan to deliver, not just attend.

rubricPoints: Asks two or three specific questions
Avoids salary and leave in the first question
redFlags: Asks something answered on the website
culturalNote: Have three questions ready; two about the work, one about the team.

prompt: Why is there a six-month gap in your CV?
translation: Mengapa ada jeda enam bulan di CV Anda?
followUps: What did you learn during that time?
How did you stay current?
skeleton: State the reason briefly and factually
Say what you did during the gap
modelAnswer: I took six months to care for a family member and to complete a cloud certification. I kept a small open-source project active and stayed in touch with two former colleagues. The situation is resolved, and I am ready to work full time.

keyPhrases.target: I kept a small open-source project active
keyPhrases.note: Shows the gap was not passive.

culturalNote: Be brief, factual, and end with availability.

prompt: You disagree with the whole panel. How do you say it?
translation: Anda tidak setuju dengan seluruh panel. Bagaimana Anda menyampaikannya?
followUps: What if they still disagree?
How do you decide when to stop pushing?
skeleton: Offer a test or a compromise
Commit to the decision once made
modelAnswer: I would start from the goal we share, then say what evidence makes me hesitate. I would propose a small test that could settle it, and if the panel still decides otherwise, I would commit and document my concern so we can revisit it with data.

keyPhrases.target: a small test that could settle it
keyPhrases.note: Turns disagreement into a decision mechanism.

culturalNote: Disagree and commit, with the concern written down.
